text: Not every interference with the enjoyment of land will be classed as a nuisance.
Describe the essential elements of private nuisance. Assess the validity of the statement above.
Describe the rules under which one person may be held vicariously liable for the tort of another.
Assess the extent to which vicarious liability is justifiable. [25]
A purely social relationship should never give rise to liability for a negligent misstatement.
Describe the elements of liability for negligent misstatement. Assess the validity of the statement
above. [25]
Section B
Andy is an experienced mountain climber. He is planning a climbing holiday. While he is preparing
for the holiday he attends a medical appointment with Doctor West, to check that he has recovered
fully from an injury to his left knee sustained on a previous climb.
Doctor West examines his left knee and tells Andy that he is fit to climb. Andy asks whether he
should have any further tests but Doctor West tells him that these are not necessary.
During the first day of climbing, Andy’s left knee suddenly fails to support his weight and he falls.
He is rescued and taken to the nearest hospital. The doctor who treats him tells him he has a
serious injury to his arm and a mild concussion. He is informed that his left knee had not fully
healed and the injury is now so severe that it is unlikely that he will be able to climb again.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in relation to negligence. [25]
Liam has recently opened a restaurant in Barchester. In order to increase sales, he decides to
deliver a menu to every house in a large group of housing which is located near his restaurant.
Marie owns one of these houses. She is trying to sell it and there is a ‘For Sale’ sign just inside the
entrance to her garden. The sign was erected by Tom, who is selling the house for Marie.
Liam delivers a menu to Marie’s house. There is a strong wind which blows the sign down and it
hits Liam. He sustains a head injury and also drops the bag of menus which blow away and are
now unusable.
Advise the parties as to their rights, responsibilities and remedies in relation to occupiers’ liability.
Priti has been growing a variety of fruit and vegetables in her garden for the last few years. She
has installed a system in her garden to collect rainwater in a series of large containers. The
containers are lined up next to the fence between Priti’s garden and her neighbour Bilal’s garden.
Priti has not been spending time in her garden as she has been busy at work and she has not
noticed that all of the containers are full. Following a period of heavy rain, the water overflows
from the containers and floods Bilal’s garden. His flowerbeds are destroyed and the engine of his
expensive lawnmower is damaged.
Advise the parties as to their rights and responsibilities in relation to Rylands v Fletcher. [25]
